goal: The Agassiz-Harrison Museum & Visitor Centre sits on 13,000 photographs, military stories that have never been told online, agricultural history that connects directly to the Fraser Valley identity, and a local personality archive that most regional communities would trade a lot to have. The goal of the next ninety days is not to get more followers. It is to convert online discovery into in-person visits by getting that material in front of the families, young couples, local residents, and school groups who do not yet know the museum exists or what is inside it. The digital assessment confirmed the foundation is solid: a 4.6-star Google rating from 125 reviews, strong technical performance, and number-one rankings for every branded search term. What is missing is volume and structure. The content goes out at a reasonable pace but lacks the pillar organisation that makes a small team's effort compound over time, the video formats that platforms now reward with reach, and the FAQ-style content that AI search tools use to answer questions about what to do in Agassiz and Harrison Hot Springs. This plan fixes all three in sequence, using what the museum already has: the archives, the Canva setup, and Maria's commitment to doing this properly.
